title: Conjugation of GABARAP to ATG9A Compartments
author: Elisabeth Holzer
materials: Analyze proteins by SDS-PAGE using a 15% gel.
Detect GABARAP and ATG9A by Western blotting.

steps.title: Isolate ATG9A compartments
steps.instruction: Isolate ATG9A‑containing compartments (or MOCK preparations) from HAP1 wild‑type cells.

steps.title: Bind compartments to GFP‑Trap beads
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL GFP‑Trap agarose beads (ChromoTek, Cat# GTA‑20) to the isolated compartments, then mix on a rotating wheel overnight at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL GFP‑Trap agarose beads (ChromoTek, Cat# GTA‑20).

steps.title: Wash beads twice
steps.instruction: Wash the beads twice with 200 µL Reaction Buffer (25 mM HEPES, pH 7.5; 150 mM NaCl; 1 mM DTT).

steps.title: Prepare lipidation reaction mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a reaction mix with the following final concentrations: 2 mM ATP, 1 mM MgCl₂, 250 nM human ATG12‑ATG5‑ATG16L1 complex, 250 nM mouse ATG7, 250 nM human ATG3, 500 nM GABARAPΔL117 mutant (use full‑length GABARAP as a negative control). Include synthetic liposomes as a positive control (20.2 % DOPC, 1.7 % DOPS, 43.2 % DOPE, 33.6 % cholesterol, 1.3 % sphingomyelin).

steps.title: Incubate reaction at 30 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the bead‑bound compartments with the prepared reaction mix at 30 °C for 3 hours (03:00:00).

steps.title: Wash beads once
steps.instruction: Wash the beads once with 200 µL Reaction Buffer (25 mM HEPES, pH 7.5; 150 mM NaCl; 1 mM DTT).

steps.title: Resuspend beads in loading buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in SDS loading buffer for downstream analysis.
